# macOS `r os_logo('apple')`

| Install the following tools to build *{{< var PROGRAM_NAME >}}* |
| :-- |
| *XCode* {{< var MIN_APPLECLANG_REQUIRED >}} or higher |
| *CMake* {{< var CMAKE_MINIMUM_REQUIRED_VERSION >}} or higher |
| *create-dmg* |
| *Homebrew* |
| *R* from CRAN (optional) |
| *Quarto* (optional) |
| *POEdit* (optional) |

To install Homebrew:

```{.bash}
/bin/bash -c  \
"$(curl -fsSL \
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
```

To install *CMake* and *create-dmg*:

```{.bash}
brew install cmake
brew install create-dmg
```

If you get errors about not finding a CXX compiler, run this:

```{.bash}
sudo xcode-select --reset
```

If you are notarizing the app locally, then add a notarization keychain to your system
(`APPLE_ID` should be set to your Apple account, usually your email address).
This only needs to be done once:

```{.bash}
APPLE_ID=
xcrun notarytool store-credentials --apple-id ${APPLE_ID}
```

When prompted, set the keychain profile to a meaningful name and enter your 10-digit organization ID as the team ID.
Then enter your app-specific password.
(You can get that from Apple's developer website.)

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Download *wxWidgets* {-}

```{.bash}
git clone https://github.com/wxWidgets/wxWidgets.git --recurse-submodules
```

This should be cloned into a folder next to *{{< var PROGRAM_NAME >}}*.

## Build *{{< var PROGRAM_NAME >}}* {-}

```{.bash include="build-commands.txt" start-line=11 end-line=20}
```

::: {.tipsection data-latex=""}
To create a debug build, pass `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` during the configuration stage, and `--config Debug` during the build stage.
You can also pass `-DENABLE_SANITIZERS=TRUE` to enable AddressSanitizer support in debug builds.

If you need to build with local modifications in Git submodules, add `-DALLOW_DIRTY_SUBMODULES=ON` to bypass the clean-check validation.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Code sign {-}

::: {.tipsection data-latex=""}
The following steps are only required if you are distributing builds outside CI, your local machine, or Eclipse's infrastructure.
:::

If code signing locally, do the following:

(`ORG_ID` should be set to your 10-digit Apple developer organization ID and `KEYCHAIN_PROFILE` should be the keychain profile connected to your Apple ID):

```{.bash}
ORG_ID=
KEYCHAIN_PROFILE=

cd installers/macos/release

codesign --force --verbose=2 --options runtime \
         --timestamp --sign ${ORG_ID} ./"Readability Studio.app"

codesign --verify --verbose=2 ./"Readability Studio.app"
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Mac App Store build {-}

::: {.tipsection data-latex=""}
This is a separate pipeline from direct distribution above.
It uses a different signing identity, an entitlements file, no notarization, and a different packaging and upload step.
Only follow this section if submitting to the Mac App Store.
For direct distribution, skip to *Build the DMG image* below.
:::

Configure and build with `APP_STORE_BUILD` enabled.
This disables the in-app "Check for Updates" feature (the App Store handles update checks itself):

```{.bash}
cmake -S . -B ./build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DAPP_STORE_BUILD=ON
cmake --build ./build --target all -j4 --config Release
```

Sign the app with the `AppStore.entitlements` file at the repo root.
This is what puts the app inside the App Sandbox that the Mac App Store requires.
`ORG_ID` here must be an **Apple Distribution** identity.
This is a different certificate than the Developer ID identity used for direct distribution above.
It must be generated separately in your Apple Developer account.

```{.bash}
ORG_ID=

cd installers/macos/release

codesign --force --verbose=2 --options runtime --timestamp \
         --entitlements ../../AppStore.entitlements \
         --sign ${ORG_ID} ./"Readability Studio.app"

codesign --verify --verbose=2 ./"Readability Studio.app"
```

App Store builds are not notarized.
(Skip the notarization steps below.)
Instead, package the signed app as an installer component with `productbuild`.
Sign it with a **Mac Installer Distribution** identity.
This is a third, separate certificate from the two above, also generated in your Apple Developer account.

```{.bash}
INSTALLER_ORG_ID=

productbuild --component "Readability Studio.app" /Applications \
             --sign ${INSTALLER_ORG_ID} \
             ReadabilityStudio.pkg
```

Upload `ReadabilityStudio.pkg` to App Store Connect with *Transporter*, a standalone app from the Mac App Store (not part of Xcode).
Drag the file in, run *Verify* from its menu, then click *Deliver*.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
For a fully scripted/CI upload instead of the Transporter app, use the [App Store Connect API](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreconnectapi) with a JSON Web Token.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Build the DMG image {-}

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
If you build the "Release" version of *{{< var PROGRAM_NAME >}}*, then the *CMake* build process will copy "{{< var PROGRAM_NAME >}}.app" into `r menu(c('installers', 'macos', 'release'))`.
:::

Go to `r menu(c('installers', 'macos'))` and run the following
(the final argument is the folder whose contents are copied into the image,
so the DMG is written one level above it):

```{.bash}
test -f ReadabilityStudio.dmg && rm ReadabilityStudio.dmg
create-dmg \
  --volname "Readability Studio Installer" \
  --volicon "../../app-logo.icns"          \
  --background "../../app-logo.png"        \
  --window-pos 200 120                     \
  --window-size 800 400                    \
  --icon-size 100                          \
  --icon "Readability Studio.app" 200 190          \
  --hide-extension "Readability Studio.app"        \
  --app-drop-link 600 185                  \
  "ReadabilityStudio.dmg"                  \
  "release/"
```

If notarizing locally, then sign, notarize, staple, and verify the DMG image:

```{.bash}
codesign --force --verbose=2 --sign ${ORG_ID} ./ReadabilityStudio.dmg
codesign --verify --verbose=2 ./ReadabilityStudio.dmg
hdiutil verify ./ReadabilityStudio.dmg
xcrun notarytool submit ./ReadabilityStudio.dmg \
  --keychain-profile ${KEYCHAIN_PROFILE}        \
  --wait

xcrun stapler staple ./ReadabilityStudio.dmg

xcrun spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature \
            --ignore-cache --verbose=2 ./ReadabilityStudio.dmg
```

If you get a notarization error, run the following
(`GUID` will be the unique ID that the submission process just displayed):

```{.bash}
xcrun notarytool log ${GUID} --keychain-profile ${KEYCHAIN_PROFILE}
```
